study: Does the live overnight book (top-20 12-1 momentum, close -> next open) hold up on 2000-2015 data, which no study has used, and is any of it more than market beta?
registered_at: 2026-10-04, before any pre-2016 stock data is fetched for this study
why: Skeptic review 2026-10-02 (SKEPTIC_REVIEW_2026-10-02.md section 1): the overnight edge is UNPROVEN; the settling test is a pre-2016 rerun. On 2016-2026 the book is mostly beta (IS beta 1.34; hedged +0.8 bp IS / +5.4 bp OOS, t 0.3 / 1.4, overnight_hedge_intraday.py). Every 2016-2026 period has now been looked at, so new evidence must come from new years.

frozen_book.rule: exactly the live/backtest rule in tools/studies/overnight_hedge_intraday.py: on each session t, eligible = raw close >= $5 AND ADV20 (20-day mean of close x volume, min 15 days) >= $50M AND finite 12-1 momentum; pick the 20 highest m = cf[t-21]/cf[t-252] - 1; equal weight; hold close(t) -> open(t+1); skip nights with fewer than 30 eligible names (counted)
frozen_book.cost: 4 bp per night round trip (same as the 2016-2026 study); the SPY hedge leg costs 2.26 bp x h
frozen_book.no_changes: no parameter of the book is changed, tuned or chosen on this data

data.source: Yahoo daily bars via yfinance, auto_adjust=False, actions=True, repair=False (frozen), 1998-06-01..today (warm-up for the 252-day momentum and ADV; to today because Yahoo split-adjusts for every split to date, so the full split history is needed for the raw-price rule), for every symbol in the 2016-2026 panel (lh_cache panel syms) plus SPY. Every fetch failure is logged; HTTP 429/timeouts are retried; the count of symbols with no data is reported. Each symbol gets a status (ok / not_found / error); symbols empty in the batch download are retried singly; check refuses to run while any symbol is in error.
data.prices: Yahoo Open/High/Low/Close are split-adjusted, not dividend-adjusted. Raw price for the $5 rule = Yahoo Close x the product of all split ratios AFTER that date (point-in-time). Dollar volume = Yahoo Close x Yahoo Volume (split-invariant). cf (the momentum ranking series) = forward-filled Yahoo Adj Close, to match the Alpaca panel (adjustment=all).
data.overnight_return: ON = (Open(t+1) + Dividend(t+1)) / Close(t) - 1, where Dividend is Yahoo's split-adjusted cash dividend with ex-date t+1 (0 otherwise); the same for SPY. This matches the panel's dividend-inclusive returns.
data.bad_data_rules: Applied to picks, universe AND SPY. A name-night is dropped (counted) if Open(t+1) or Close(t) is missing or <= 0, Open(t+1)==High==Low==Close with zero volume, |ON| > 50%, or t+1 is within +/-1 trading day of a split ex-date (Yahoo split-date errors give -50%/-33%). A whole name-YEAR is dropped from picks and universe if more than 25% of its nights have ON exactly 0 (Yahoo filled the open with the prior close; KO 2000 63%). Reported: the ON==0 share by year, separately for picks and universe, and drops by rule. The name-year rule masks ON only; it is NOT an eligibility or selection input (pick slots are unchanged, so a masked pick leaves fewer than 20 names that night); masked pick slots are reported.
data.survivorship: the symbol list is names that existed in 2016-2026, so pre-2016 delistings are MISSING. This biases toward survivors. The universe-relative statistic (S2) is the main defence: picks and universe are both survivors.
data.abort: if fewer than 60% of nights 2000-2015 have >= 30 eligible names, report coverage only and draw no verdict

period: 2000-01-03..2015-12-31 (book nights), split by date into P1 2000-2007 and P2 2008-2015

statistics.S1_alpha: book net of 4 bp per night, regressed on SPY overnight (dividend-inclusive) over the period: S1 = intercept minus 2.26 bp x the fitted beta (cost of the hedge leg) = alpha after beta and all costs, bp/night
statistics.S2_relative_alpha: (picks overnight mean minus the equal-weighted overnight mean of ALL eligible names the same night, gross) regressed on SPY overnight: S2 = intercept (the ranking's information net of its own residual beta; S2 has beta ~0.44 on 2016-2026)
statistics.SE: for each intercept, SE = max(plain OLS SE, Newey-West 5 lags, Newey-West 9 lags) (the series are negatively autocorrelated, so NW alone would shrink the SE)
statistics.decides: ONLY S1 and S2 decide. Everything else is information.
statistics.information_only: unhedged net mean/t; S1 with the fixed 2017-2021 hedge h = 1.34; S1 with a point-in-time trailing 252-night beta hedge; realised beta in P1, P2, all; S1 at 20 bp cost for 2000-2002 (1/16-tick era); eligible names per night (median, min); nights skipped; worst night, CVaR 1%, max drawdown; per-year S1 and S2; pick overlap with the panel in the data-source check

power: Before reading any mean: SE(S1) and SE(S2) over 2000-2015; MDE = 2.84 x SE. If MDE(S1) > 5 bp, S1 is UNDERPOWERED (no verdict on alpha); same for S2. Pre-stated expectation (skeptic, from 2016-2026 nightly SD ~122 bp): SE ~1.9-3 bp, MDE ~7-9 bp, so S1 is LIKELY UNDERPOWERED and the likely outcome for alpha is UNPROVEN; S2 may still be decided if the ranking effect is large.

pass.EDGE_REPLICATES: S2 powered, S2 > 0 with t >= 2.0 over 2000-2015, S2 > 0 in both P1 and P2, and the survivorship calibration does not void it
pass.ALPHA: S1 powered, S1 > 0 with t >= 2.0 over 2000-2015, S1 > 0 in both P1 and P2, and the survivorship calibration does not void it
pass.reading: EDGE_REPLICATES + ALPHA: the overnight edge is more than beta; grounds (with real auction fills) to discuss a larger live account. EDGE_REPLICATES only: the ranking has information but the money is mostly beta; keep $100 and consider the hedge. ALPHA only: alpha without a ranking effect relative to the universe means the book's excess comes from the eligible universe itself (liquid $5+ names vs SPY), not the momentum ranking; report as UNEXPLAINED, no action. Neither (or underpowered): the overnight book is unproven beyond a leveraged index bet; say so plainly. Multiplicity: two decisive tests, each needs t >= 2.0 AND both halves positive; no Bonferroni beyond that, stated.

data_source_check: Same nights 2017-01-13..2021-12-31 and the same symbols (only where Yahoo returns data): Yahoo-built book vs Alpaca-panel book. Passes only if the mean nightly difference is <= 1 bp with |t| < 2 AND the nightly book-return correlation is >= 0.9; pick overlap is reported. If it fails, 2000-2015 is unreliable: no verdict.
no_retuning: nothing is changed after data is seen; any later variant is a new pre-registration
prior: moderate for S2: Lou, Polk and Skouras (2019) find momentum profits accrue overnight in 1993-2013 US stocks; weak for S1 given the 2016-2026 hedged result
caveats: Yahoo open prices before ~2005 can be unreliable
$50M ADV is nominal, so fewer names qualify in early years
auction costs in 2000-2015 were higher than 4 bp; the hedged money result is therefore an upper bound
S1 at 4 bp understates early-era costs (20 bp shown for 2000-2002 as information)
amended: 2026-10-04, before any pre-2016 data or script, per the skeptic's FIX FIRST (3 blockers, 5 fix-first, minors), all applied
survivorship_calibration: On data already in hand (Alpaca panel, which includes inactive names from 2018): compute S1 and S2 for 2018-2026 twice, (a) full panel, (b) only names that still have bars in the panel's last month (survivors). Report the gap (b - a) for each. If |gap(S2)| >= half of the 2000-2015 S2 point estimate, S2 is NO VERDICT (survivorship could explain it); same for S1. A second calibration uses survivors = symbols Yahoo still serves (the actual pre-2016 selection); the verdict is voided if EITHER gap fails the half-of-estimate rule.
process: the script is committed and reviewed by the skeptic BEFORE the pre-2016 fetch
amended_2: 2026-10-04, before any pre-2016 fetch, after the skeptic's script review (225e0d4): per-symbol fetch status, second survivorship calibration, fetch to today, name-year rule clarified
